A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FaSTA* study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original FaSTA* quality and execution-time measurements, component ablations, and appendix experiments, including Table 3, Figure 3, and Table 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Complex-Edit evaluation, restricted-toolset comparisons, caching comparisons, and further analyses.

M1.justification: The induction, verification, subroutine selection, and local A* fallback procedures remain unchanged. The new semantic-bucketing wording describes qualitative activation rules already present in v1 Table 7 and Appendix P; the corresponding rule table, algorithms, and prompts retain their substance.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on a subset of the independent Complex-Edit benchmark (Table 4), extending the evaluated image data within the existing multi-turn editing domain and 1-8-subtask range. The CoSTA* benchmark, qualitative MagicBrush examples, and external induction data are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds a direct-cache comparator (Table 14) and GPT-4o image editing (Table 15), substantially extending comparisons beyond the original planners and editors. Gemini 2.0, already compared qualitatively in v1 Figure 13, also receives a quantitative comparison. The main Table 3 comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments restrict FaSTA* and CoSTA* to the baselines' toolsets and supported subtasks (Tables 10-11), introducing important comparison controls. Section 5.3 also tests Qwen 2.5VL 3B for subroutine selection. The original benchmark and human-scoring protocol are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds the smaller-selector ablation, cost-quality learning trajectory, amortized overhead analysis, fallback-reason and category breakdowns, and toolset-matched and caching analyses (Section 5.3; Appendices C, D, J). These substantially extend investigation of robustness, efficiency, and the source of the gains beyond v1's existing ablations.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix K newly reports evaluator-score variance of 0.07; v1 Appendix I supplies scoring rules and averaging formulas without this statistic. No additional seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is reported.

E6.justification: The main Table 3 scores and original ablation values are retained, but substantial new results appear. Complex-Edit results report 55.12 seconds and 0.87 accuracy for FaSTA*, versus 78.27 seconds and 0.89 for CoSTA* (Table 4). Table 15 reports quality scores of 0.91, 0.78, and 0.74 for FaSTA*, Gemini 2.0, and GPT-4o. Further tables add learning, fallback, restricted-toolset, and caching outcomes.

T1.justification: The A* cost and heuristic definitions, net-benefit acceptance criterion, and accuracy-aggregation formulas retain their mathematical substance. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same symbolic-subroutine learning and adaptive fast-slow planning claims, including 49.3% cost savings with 3.2% quality degradation relative to CoSTA*. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendices C, D, and J substantially expand interpretation through overhead amortization, explanations of fallback despite apparently applicable rules, attribution of gains to planning rather than tool access, and generalization versus memorization. Appendix C.1 also newly asserts no quality degradation, more strongly than its Table 7 decline from 0.93 to 0.91 supports.

D1.justification: New Appendix O explicitly assigns LLM roles, including GPT-4o for chain generation, and Appendix J specifies the cache's 5% matching tolerance. However, Appendix O names GPT-o1 for subroutine selection while Section 4.3 still names GPT-4o, creating an implementation ambiguity rather than establishing a model switch. The project link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion and citations for BLIP-3o, BLIP3o-NEXT, and MuLan. The bibliography also drops references including DeblurGAN and Real-ESRGAN. The central positioning relative to CoSTA* and in-context reinforcement learning remains intact.

P1.justification: Limited prose edits accompany expanded appendix subsections, updated affiliation and conference-header text, and changed citation and heading styles. Most existing exposition, section sequence, and prompt content remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds eight tables (Tables 4, 7-11, 14-15) and the learning-trajectory Figure 9. It also adopts conference formatting, relocates and resizes retained displays, and consolidates algorithm placement. These constitute substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Quantitative external-benchmark validation and the toolset-matched and direct-cache comparisons address important gaps in v1's evidence for generalization and the source of efficiency gains. Learning-cost and fallback analyses also clarify practical tradeoffs. These validation gains substantially improve the paper, although underspecified new protocols, conflicting selector-model descriptions, and overstated quality-preservation language limit the improvement.
